summary.text: 右 is the common character for “right,” including the right hand and right-hand side. One account says it developed from the whole sign 又, reused for a word meaning “right” because the words may have sounded alike; the old name and sound match are unestablished. Other accounts read 又 and 口 as parts of a hand-and-mouth or ritual scene.

formation.text: The formation remains disputed. One account treats 又 as a right hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, associating the graph with ritual service and assistance. Another says 右 was first written with 又 as a whole sign for “right,” then gained 口 as a distinguishing mark. A phonosemantic analysis assigns 又 a sound role and 口 a meaning role. The evidence does not resolve these proposals or establish a graphic transition sequence.

components.text: One interpretation treats 又 as a right hand in a ritual scene; another as a whole sign borrowed for “right”; a phonosemantic account assigns it a sound role. These analyses are distinct and disputed.

sound_limitation.text: The cited readings permit sound comparisons, but they do not independently establish 又 as a component of 右 or prove that it has a phonetic role there.

sound.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart entries have similar Old Chinese forms; the comparison alone does not establish a phonetic role within 右.
The selected readings differ in Middle Chinese tone category and reading form.
Both are listed with the same modern Mandarin reading; this match alone does not establish their historical relationship.

components.text: The received Shuowen account reads 口 as a mouth acting with the hand. A competing account identifies it as a ritual prayer vessel; another says it was added as a distinguishing mark. These analyses assign it different roles.

history.text: Catalogues list forms of 右 across oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, seal, and clerical script traditions, but do not date the cited oracle-bone specimen or establish a precise sequence of graphic changes.

The received Shuowen explanation describes a hand and mouth acting together and survives in versions with different component order. Later commentary and a competing account dispute this as the graph’s original construction; the textual variants do not resolve its formation.

One account proposes that 又 was first used as a whole sign for 右 and that 口 was added later to distinguish the graphs. Another gives 口 a ritual meaning. The supplied evidence does not settle either account or verify the proposed transition.

uncertainties.text: The evidence does not establish which recorded sense came first or a chronological chain connecting direction, assistance, blessing, ritual service, rank, west, and banquet-related use.

The proposed whole-sign borrowing account says 又 was reused to write the word for “right” because the words may have sounded alike or similarly. The old name of the depicted object and the sound match are not independently established here; this proposal does not show that 又 was a phonetic component inside 右.

senses.gloss: right; right hand or right-hand side
senses.text: The character is recorded for the right hand and right side, but the evidence does not identify either as its earliest sense.
Classical citations record uses meaning help or assist. They are not dated here well enough to establish priority or a development from the directional sense.
Dictionary records include uses for blessing or protection, without establishing their chronology or a semantic link to direction or assistance.
West is recorded as a sense of 右; the evidence does not date it or explain its relation to “right.”
High status or rank is recorded among historical uses, with no chronology or development established here.
A banquet-related use is recorded and glossed as 侑. The evidence does not establish whether this is an extension of meaning or a distinct word written with 右.
The modern political sense is recorded, but no date or account of its development is supplied.

limitations.text: The recorded senses do not establish the earliest Chinese use or a chronological semantic sequence among them.

If 又 was borrowed as a whole sign for a word meaning “right,” the written sign was reused because the words sounded alike or similarly, rather than because “also” developed into “right.” The old object-name and sound match remain unestablished here.

overview.text: 右 is the common character for “right,” including the right hand and right-hand side. One account proposes that the whole sign 又 was reused for “right” because the words may have sounded alike; the old name and sound match are unestablished. Other accounts see a hand with a mouth or ritual vessel.

components.text: 又 may depict a right hand in a ritual scene; other accounts treat it as the earlier whole sign or as a sound element within 右.
口 is read as a mouth in one traditional account, a ritual vessel in another, or a later distinguishing mark in a competing account.

relationships.text: A competing analysis treats 又 as the depiction of a right hand within a ritual scene in 右.

One analysis assigns 又 a phonetic role in 右. The supplied readings permit a sound comparison, but do not independently confirm the component identity or role; another account treats 又 as an earlier whole sign instead.
One interpretation identifies 口 as a ritual prayer vessel in 右, distinct from the account that reads it as a mouth or a differentiating mark.
A phonosemantic analysis assigns 口 a meaning contribution. The supplied account does not show that this is the same analysis as the ritual-vessel interpretation.
One account describes 口 as a later mark added to distinguish 右 from 又; the proposed graphic transition is not independently verified.
